JULY, 1950

FESTIVE OCCASIONS

THE Civic Reception in Perth's spacious City Hall was a memorable occasion, for the rustling of the silks and brocades of the ladies on their way to being received by the Lord and Lady Provost and the Bailies of the City was lost against the skirling of the pipes played by a piper in full Highland regalia. The Grand March, headed by The Dowager Lady Swaythling and the Lord Provost, started the proceedings. The display of Highland dancing by four kilted young men with their equally nimble-footed girl partners was a source of special pleasure, and later in the evening many of the English company present were emboldened themselves to try "The Gay Gordons."

The Scottish Branches' Party was an evening of full enjoyment, and after the reception by Lady MacColl and the Scottish Council, The Dowager Lady Swaythling cut the 25th Birthday Cake.
